blinding_guess.why: The snapshot never names /tf or tf2_msgs/TFMessage; both reach the bridge only at run time (client subscribe request or graph discovery), so nothing element-specific is declared that could be judged defective. The only element-relevant behaviour is the generic subscriber QoS rule, which is peer-dependent.

notes: The snapshot holds the whole rosbridge_suite repository (rosbridge_suite meta-package plus rosbridge_library, rosbridge_server, rosapi, rosapi_msgs, rosbridge_msgs, rosbridge_test_msgs, all 2.2.0); rosbridge_suite/package.xml itself is a meta-package with exec_depend only, so the code of the member packages was treated as the unit. Neither packet element is named anywhere in the snapshot (grep for tf2_msgs, TFMessage, /tf, tf_static): the topic name arrives at run time in the rosbridge protocol 'subscribe' op ('topic' required, 'type' optional; snapshot:rosbridge_library/src/rosbridge_library/capabilities/subscribe.py:209-210, 238, 270), so both elements are in neither declares nor references. The only tf2_msgs mentions are a test_depend (rosbridge_library/package.xml:45, rosbridge_test_msgs/package.xml:42) and tests naming tf2_msgs/FrameGraph, tf2_msgs/LookupTransform, tf2_msgs/GetDualQuaternionRepresentation, not the packet elements. ports[1].msg_type is null: the type is either the optional client-supplied 'type' or the first type discovered in the ROS graph for the topic (snapshot:rosbridge_library/src/rosbridge_library/internal/subscribers.py:80-95; a warning is logged if more than one type is found, and TypeConflictException is raised if the client type differs from the established one, :100-103; TopicNotEstablishedException if neither exists, :84-85). ports[0].msg_type is the packet element itself with its jazzy definition hash (sha256_normalised, a proxy for the ROS 2 type hash); the package does not declare it. Frame: rosbridge forwards messages whole without reading or setting any frame, so frame is null for both ports (TFMessage carries a frame_id per transform header in the definition, but that is not taken by this code). QoS (topic subscription path, applies to /tf when a client subscribes to it): subscribers.py:116-127 builds QoSProfile(depth=10, durability=VOLATILE, reliability=BEST_EFFORT), then, from get_publishers_info_by_topic, sets durability=TRANSIENT_LOCAL and reliability=RELIABLE if any publisher is TRANSIENT_LOCAL, then reliability=BEST_EFFORT if any publisher is BEST_EFFORT; so with no publishers it is BEST_EFFORT/VOLATILE. When a further client joins an existing subscriber (subscribers.py:184-188) the rule is re-applied but only sets TRANSIENT_LOCAL durability (without forcing RELIABLE) and BEST_EFFORT reliability. Reliability and durability are therefore peer-selected and recorded null per instructions. No deadline, lifespan or liveliness is set in code (rclpy QoSProfile then uses the RMW default deadline, i.e. no deadline), so deadline_ms is null; history depth 10 is fixed. No rate is set in code; throttle_rate (minimum ms between forwarded messages) and queue_length are client-supplied per subscription (subscribe.py:89-90, 185-186, 271-273). perm_grants: the bridge grants remote clients access to topics/services/params filtered by the configurable security globs named in values; the glob contents are configuration supplied at launch (default empty string = no filtering), not fixed in the snapshot. exclusive: none declared; the websocket server binds a TCP listening port (parameter 'port', default 9090, rosbridge_websocket.py:110, 161) but the code does not name any exclusively claimed hardware or device resource. Recovery value is package-level (server startup); the subscription path itself has no retry. launch also exposes respawn (default false, launch.xml:29).
